title: The decimals of a currency: two for the dollar, three for the dinar, none for the yen, each document rounded half up to the decimals of its own currency; built here, with the base journal kept to the decimals of the base

currency_decimals.note: Purchases in KWD (3 x 10.125 = 30.375, journal 000212 at 12.04917 = 365.993 SAR) and in JPY (3 x 1,234.5 = 3,703.5 shown as 3,704, journal 000213 at 0.02376 = 88 SAR); USD has two decimals

cases.reason: The decimals of each currency are built (WP28): zero, two or three from the catalog, and a document is rounded half up to the decimals of its own currency, as the reference system does. The journal in the base is kept to the two decimals of the base where the reference system showed 365.993 and 88. A document in the register takes up to two decimals in a quantity and a price: an amount of three decimals is refused by name.
